 Ford recalls 11,000 Lincoln vehicles. See affected models
 USA TODAY – Cars Greta Cross, USA TODAY Updated Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:51 PM UTC Add to Preferred Sources Updated Tue, October 27, 2026 at 3:51 PM UTC Ford has recalled more than 11,000 hybrid vehicles that may unexpectedly shift into neutral while driving due to corrosion in the transmission.
 Ford Motor Company estimates that 100% of the outlined vehicles are affected by the recall, according to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall report. As of Sept. 28, Ford was aware of 15 warranty claims, one field report and one customer report in the United States, the report outlines. As of Oct. 20, Ford was not aware of any accidents, fires or injuries related to the issue.
 The issue specifically lies within the transmission's park lock actuator circuit board, which is responsible for keeping a vehicle's gear shift locked in park when the brake pedal is pressed, according to PartCatalog .
 Advertisement Advertisement According to the recall report, a service wrench malfunction indicator light should illuminate on the dashboard and a popup that reads "Service Vehicle Soon" or "Shifting System Error" would appear on the display.
 Here's what to know about the Ford recall.
 A Lincoln Nautilus hybrid is offered for sale at a dealership on June 5, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. What vehicles are affected by the recall?
 The Ford recall applies to the following vehicles:
 2027 Lincoln Corsair Hybrid (63 vehicles)
 2026-2027 Lincoln Nautilus Hybrid (11,560 vehicles)
 What to do if your vehicle is recalled
 Dealerships will replace the vehicle's Integrated Park Modul for free, according to the recall report. Owners may contact Ford customer service at 1-866-436-7332. Ford's recall number is 26S75.
